extracted.intended_audience: Prospective KAKENHI applicants and research institution administrative staff (JSPS/MEXT-funded researchers and admins)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an FY2024 KAKENHI application (Fund for the Promotion of Joint International Research — International Leading Research), and complying with all JSPS/MEXT instructions, eligibility rules, ethics, financial management, and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of Research Proposal Document
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of the Research Proposal Document must be original planned by the applicant; plagiarism and/or misappropriation of the research contents of others are strictly impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with research ethics. The use of generative AI in preparation carries risks (copyright infringement, leakage of personal/confidential information) and is the researcher's responsibility to decide on appropriate usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher Initiative and Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Research using KAKENHI funds should be carried out by the researcher(s)’ own initiative and responsibility; implementation and publication of results are solely the researchers' responsibility and do not reflect the funding sector or government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers must plan and execute projects independently and ensure that outputs are attributable to their own views and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the Code of Conduct for Scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must understand and practice the Code of Conduct for Scientists (Revised Version) and related JSPS booklet on conscientious scientist attitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required to ensure quality of scientific knowledge and social trust; applicants should refer to specified sections (e.g., Responsibilities of Scientists) and integrate these principles into research conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active International Dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers are urged to disseminate research results aggressively to the international society via publications in international journals, co-authorship of international papers, presentations at international conferences, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts to increase international visibility and collaboration are expected and will be considered in the program's aim to foster international-leading researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Revised Research Proposal Document Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow the FY2024 changed structure of the Research Proposal Document intended to select proposals that contribute 'to foster researchers'; specific procedures for preparing and entering documents are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 'Procedures for Preparing and Entering a Research Proposal Document (Forms to be uploaded)' and '... (Items to be entered in the Website)'. Note: 'Status of Application and Acquisition of Research Grants' column will not appear on the PDF but is reviewed via the electronic system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and Participation (JSPS Fellows (DC))
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting FY2023, JSPS Fellows (DC) can participate in KAKENHI-funded research categories as Co-Investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check III. Instructions for Prospective Applicants 1. Procedures to be Completed Prior to Application for specifics on including JSPS Fellows (DC) as co-investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply to Correct Research Category (budget/period/aims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must choose the appropriate KAKENHI research category (e.g., Specially Promoted Research, Scientific Research (S/A/B/C), Transformative Research Area, International Leading Research, etc.) according to purpose, period, and budget ranges specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category has explicit aims, eligible team composition, project periods, and budget ranges; applicants should match project scope to category and follow any category-specific notes (e.g., extendable periods in special cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Types of Applicable Rules (Application/Assessment/Spending)
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI are governed by three types of rules: Application Rules (submission), Assessment Rules (pre-assessment/review/interim/progress assessment), and Spending Rules (use of funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions must be familiar with and follow the set of rules applicable to their role (JSPS, research institutions, researchers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Use of KAKENHI Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI must be used efficiently and effectively (e.g., communal use of purchased items), in compliance with related laws, regulations, and spending rules; research institutions are responsible for fund management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should establish accounting systems, purchase order/delivery inspection processes, internal auditing, and measures to prevent improper business transactions (e.g., inform traders of rules to prevent fraudulent accounting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year Fund Handling (carryover/extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI (Multi-year Fund) is handled as single funding for the whole research period; unused amounts can be carried over to successive fiscal years within the research period without prior authorization, and grantees may request a one-year extension in final-year carry-over cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets across fiscal-year boundaries; follow extension request procedures if needed in final year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Submission of Report on the Research Achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must submit a 'Report on the Research Achievements' via their research institution at the end of the research period; contents are compiled and made public on databases (e.g., KAKEN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-submission without justifiable reason leads to penalties including ineligibility for future grants, suspension/cancellation of current grants, orders to return funds, and public disclosure. Institutions are responsible for ensuring timely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for Violation of Laws/Falsehood in Application
rubrics_metrics.description: If serious falsehoods are found in application documents or laws/regulations are violated, grant delivery may be suspended or cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide truthful and complete information; misrepresentation can trigger cancellation and further sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of Unreasonable Duplication and Excessive Overconcentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must avoid 'Unreasonable Duplication' (redundant allocation of multiple funds to the same research project) and 'Excessive Concentration' (allocation of funds to a researcher/group beyond effective/efficient use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on funding applications is shared cross-ministerially (e-Rad); when submitting multiple applications, clearly state differences between projects to avoid being judged duplication. Cases of duplication/excessive concentration may lead to rejection, cancellation, or budget reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Unreasonable Duplication (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unreasonable Duplication includes: simultaneous applications to multiple funds for substantially the same project that are redundantly adopted; re-applying for essentially the same already-adopted project; duplication in use of research funds across projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must avoid submitting substantively identical projects to different funders/agencies and must disclose overlaps and differences explicitly in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Excessive Overconcentration (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive Concentration occurs when total funds allotted to a researcher/group exceed what can be used efficiently within the research period, given abilities and methods, allocated effort (time%), or lead to unnecessary expensive purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests should be proportional to effort, personnel capacity, and realistic equipment needs; avoid requesting funds that cannot be effectively spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of Improper Grant Spending / Fraudulent Grant Acquisition / Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper Grant Spending: using funds for other purposes (fictitious transactions, overcharging, violating funding conditions). Fraudulent Grant Acquisition: obtaining funds by deception (applying under another's name, false entries). Research Misconduct: fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, or failure of duty of care in published research achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are used to determine disciplinary actions; examples are provided (e.g., forged invoices, false attendance sheets, manipulated data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and Suspension Periods for Improper Spending, Fraud, and Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties include suspension from receiving KAKENHI for specified periods (tables define different periods depending on type and seriousness), orders to return grants, cancellation of grants, and public disclosure of case details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables specify suspension durations (e.g., misappropriation for personal gain: 10 years; other cases vary from 1 to 5 years). Research misconduct suspension varies by role (responsible authors, other authors, non-authors) and degree of maliciousness/impact, with ranges up to 10 years. Sharp reprimands for subcritical cases may be administered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Disclosure and Cross-Agency Sharing of Misconduct/Impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlines of improper spending, fraudulent acquisition, and research misconduct (including names, institutions, project details, measures taken) may be made public and shared with other funding agencies, potentially restricting applications to other funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious cases may lead to broad restrictions across other competitive research funds; investigators should be aware of cross-ministerial information sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Obligations for Management and Audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions must manage KAKENHI funds appropriately (accounting, audits) and comply with guidelines on management/audit of public research funds and guidelines for responding to research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If institutional systems are inadequate, measures (e.g., reduction in indirect cost support) may be taken. Institutions should implement system improvements and ensure compliance with implementation standards and misconduct response guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Improper Grant Spending / Fraud / Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples are provided (e.g., forged fictitious transactions with traders, false invoices, false attendance sheets to siphon funds, visiting destinations not on approved itinerary for unrelated cooperative research; manipulating/forging experimental data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate behaviors deemed misappropriation, fraudulent acquisition, or misconduct, and emphasize that even expenditures intended for research can be misappropriation if fictitious or falsified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Deposit/Share Bioresources (NBRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers are asked to deposit available bioresources developed by KAKENHI projects (limited to NBRP-targeted resources) and cooperate with NBRP collecting activities; use of already-collected NBRP resources is recommended for efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit is a procedure to approve use/preservation/provision without transferring rights; deposit agreements can include usage restrictions/quotion requirements. A list of NBRP core bases is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Export Control Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers and institutions must take systematic measures to prevent research achievements with potential military diversion from going to WMD developers, terrorists, or dubious actors; exports/provision of regulated cargo or technology require permission under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of technology includes design drawings, specs, manuals, samples, prototypes, storage media, and technical assistance (seminars, training). Prior permission may be required when providing 'List rules' technologies to non-residents or abroad, and catch-all regulations may apply. Consult METI guidance and the provided links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict Implementation of UNSC Resolution 2321
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions must strictly implement UNSC Resolution 2321 concerning restrictions on 'scientific and technical cooperation' with DPRK (excluding medical exchanges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resolution broadens what counts as restricted cooperation beyond items regulated by the Foreign Exchange Act; institutions should exercise caution in all cooperative activities and consult MOFA resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement of Treatment of Doctoral Students Employed as RAs
rubrics_metrics.description: When employing doctoral students as research assistants, institutions must set hourly wages according to job nature/content based on institutional standards, pay according to actual work hours under proper labor management, avoid overloading students, and ensure balance with their research/study time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenditures necessary to employ RAs should be recorded as direct expenses in applications; school rules may need revision to ensure proper compensation and labor management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing and Supporting URAs and Management Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions are encouraged to secure URAs and management personnel with certain lengths of fixed-term employment (around five years or longer) and build career paths, using indirect expenses and other funds as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should support training/enrollment in URA programs, consider indirect expense use for personnel development, and strive to improve conditions to attract qualified management staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of Gender Equality and Diverse Researcher Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS will take into account efforts to promote participation and advancement of female researchers and to expand the range of human resources in science and technology; institutions are urged to support environments that help researchers continue through life events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JSPS established 'Basic Guidelines for Promoting Gender Equality' and resources (e.g., CHEERS!) to support balancing research and life events. Efforts to consider sex differences in research implementation where relevant are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of Research Ethics Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to complete research ethics education courses or equivalent prior to application (referenced in TOC: 'Completion of Research Ethics Education Course or Other etc.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check III. Instructions for Prospective Applicants for the required types and proofs of completion and ensure documentation is current before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of Researcher Information in researchmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register researcher information in researchmap as part of application procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the registration instructions and use the researchmap service; links and support contacts are provided in the inquiries section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Parallel Grant Application/Receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: There are restrictions on submitting/receiving parallel grants; applicants must disclose other competitive funding and clearly state differences to avoid being judged as unreasonable duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False or untruthful entries regarding status of other applications/acquisitions (name/title/period/amount/effort/affiliation) may lead to rejection/cancellation. Information is shared across ministries; fully inform affiliated institutions of all relevant funding and side jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for Preparing and Entering Research Proposal Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must prepare application forms (Research Proposal Document) in accordance with the provided 'Procedures for Preparing and Entering a Research Proposal Document' including both items to be entered on the website and items to be uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow templates/forms, observe specifications for uploaded PDFs, and consult the JSPS website for downloads. Check how elements (e.g., 'Status of Application and Acquisition of Research Grants') are handled in the electronic system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation to Review (Obligation to Review Processes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/researchers may be required to cooperate with review processes (peer review and other assessment activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section on 'Cooperation to Review' in instructions; institutions and researchers should be prepared to supply requested information and participate in review-related activities as asked by JSPS.
